preconditions.description: Input consists of two integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 50) and k (1 ≤ k ≤ min{10^18, l}), where l is the number of valid permutations for n.
Input is a single line containing exactly two space-separated integers n and k.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= int(n) for x in stdout.strip().split()) and len(stdout.strip().split()) == int(n)
postconditions.description: Output is a permutation of length n, where each element is an integer between 1 and n (inclusive).

postconditions.expression:
def is_fixed_permutation(p):
    n = len(p)
    p = [int(x) - 1 for x in p]  # convert to 0-based
    cycles = []
    visited = [False] * n
    for i in range(n):
        if not visited[i]:
            cycle = []
            x = i
            while not visited[x]:
                visited[x] = True
                cycle.append(x)
                x = p[x]
            if len(cycle) > 1:
                cycle_sorted = sorted(cycle, key=lambda x: -p[x])
                cycle_reordered = [p[x] for x in cycle_sorted]
                cycle_reordered_sorted = sorted(cycle_reordered)
                cycle_reordered_sorted_str = ''.join(map(str, cycle_reordered_sorted))
                cycle_original_str = ''.join(map(str, cycle))
                if cycle_reordered_sorted_str != cycle_original_str:
                    return False
    return True

is_fixed_permutation(stdout.strip().split())
postconditions.description: The output permutation p satisfies the condition that its standard cyclic representation, when parentheses are removed, equals p itself. This means p is invariant under the described transformation.
The output permutation is the k-th permutation in lexicographic order that satisfies the invariant condition (Q2).
